svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.12.3.3 Deleterious Debris and Boulders
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.12.3.3 Deleterious Debris and Boulders
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.12 EXCAVATION
Deleterious Debris and Boulders

g.text: free of deleterious debris and of
The 600 mm next to the foundation, Sentence (1)
Concrete block insulated on the exterior
Concrete block with a slip plane material
Where ice lensing backfill is permitted, Sentence (3)

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Backfill within 600 mm (23⅝″) of the
foundation is free of deleterious debris and
boulders larger than 250 mm (9 13/16″) diam.
Note A-9.12.3.3.(1) lists, among others: organic
and other material subject to decomposition and
compaction, materials that will off-gas and may
pose a health hazard, and materials incompatible
with those used in the foundations, footings or
drainage.
Except as in Sentence (3), backfill does not
contain pyritic material or material
susceptible to ice lensing in concentrations
that will damage the building
To a degree that would adversely affect its
stability or the performance of assemblies.
Backfill with material of any concentration
susceptible to ice lensing is permitted where
foundation walls are
(a) cast-in-place concrete, (b) concrete block
insulated on the exterior, or (c) concrete block
protected from the backfill by a material that
serves as a slip plane.
Drawn: walls and backfill cut through. In A the stones are on the cut face. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.12.3.3. (page 9-108)
